headline: Claude Fable 5 turns the day into an agent-workflow arms race, with skills, evals, and real business workflows taking center stage.
executiveSummary: Claude Fable 5 is the dominant platform signal: official launch posts, benchmark claims, Code Arena results, Agent Arena results, and enterprise evals all point to a step-change in long-horizon coding and knowledge work.

The builder stack is shifting from prompts to reusable systems: loops, skills, repo-audit plans, context graphs, Deep Agents, and workflow orchestration are the practical patterns showing up across X and GitHub.

Evaluation is getting more operational: FrontierCode, Agents' Last Exam, Claw-SWE-Bench, and Arbor all focus on whether agents can handle maintainable code, economically useful work, and long-horizon research loops.

The business thread is less about generic AI apps and more about distribution, integration, and SMB/operator leverage: OpenAI's confidential S-1, iMessage AI assistants, applied AI moats, SMB data, and founder research agents are the strongest market signals.

GitHub momentum is skill-heavy but security-sensitive, with agent-skills, pm-skills, superpowers, shadcn/improve, Hivemind, context-mode, and SkillSpector showing the next layer of agent infrastructure.

items.title: Agent spend guard
items.body: Fable 5 burns a week of $200-plan quota in a day and developers only find out when they hit the wall — the 'too expensive' thread on HN is people who cannot see where their tokens go. Solo builders and small teams running coding agents all day would pay for a local proxy that meters burn per task, flags runaway loops before they eat the quota, and routes mechanical work to cheaper models. Easybilling just claimed the billing side of usage-based AI products; nobody owns the cost-control side of the agent stack yet.

items.title: Bring-your-own-agent code review
items.body: CodeRabbit is throttling annual subscribers to two reviews an hour, and the Ask HN thread shows working engineers shopping for a replacement the same day. Teams already paying for review bots would pay for one that runs on the Claude or Codex subscription they already have instead of a metered SaaS — bring-your-own-agent review with repo-aware checklists. Claude Code v2.1.172 shipping nested sub-agents (5 levels deep) makes the fan-out — one reviewer per file, a synthesizer on top — a weekend build rather than an infra project.
